messages.author: 0cc7a87e6148a7b2
messages.subject: link=1 in control.predictor
parts:
Hi,

How can I set link=1 in control predictor when we have two likelihoods? 
I tried the following example, but link=1 is not working for gamma model.  

res.zy <- inla(r ~ 0 + z.b0 + y.b0 + f(i.z, model=spde) +f(i.y, copy='i.z', fixed=FALSE),
               family=c('binomial', 'gamma'),
               control.family=list(list(link="logit"),list(link="log")),
               data=inla.stack.data(stk.zy), control.compute=list(config=TRUE,dic=TRUE),
               control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy), compute=TRUE,link=1))
 
Thanks in advance.
Soraia

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] link=1 in control.predictor
parts:
For multi-likelihood models, you need to set the link parameter to a vector, where each value indicates which of the link functions to use, for each data/prediction point.
E.g. if your response matrix has 3 rows for likelihood 1 and 5 rows for likelihood 2, followed by 4 rows of NA for predicting two points on the linked scale for each likelihood, link should be set to
c(1,1,1,2,2,2,2,2,1,1,2,2)

link=1 is just shorthand for “apply the first link function to everything”.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] link=1 in control.predictor
parts: Just one more question: shouldn’t exp(res.zy$summary.linear.predictor[iy.v,1]) give the same result as res.zy$summary.fitted.values[iy.v,1] when the link function is “log” (assuming that the link was correctly defined in control.predictor)?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] link=1 in control.predictor
parts:
The quantiles should match (up to numerical computing differences), but not the posterior mean. E(exp(x)) is not the same as exp(E(x)). So to check your code, look at the 0.5quant column instead of the mean.

Finn

parts: More specifically, Jensen’s inequality reveals that exp(E(x)) < E(exp(x)), unless x is a constant.

Finn
